stream.transport: SSE under existing authenticated event endpoints; same canonical event sources as chat/history
stream.dedupe: Persist cursor per streamId; discard duplicate eventId; sequence is authoritative, timestamps are not ordering keys.
stream.lateEvents: An event at or below accepted sequence is retained only as historical evidence, never an operational animation or state regression.
stream.gap: On sequence gap freeze operational animations, mark stale, request replay; do not infer intermediate success.
stream.reconnect: Reconnect after 1, 2, 4, 8, then 15 seconds while visible; send Last-Event-ID. On expired cursor fetch authoritative snapshot with sequence watermark before replay.
stream.fallback: After 30 seconds disconnected show persistent notice and poll canonical snapshots every 15 seconds while visible; never synthesize activity.
stream.aggregation: Maintain full ordered event evidence; repaint at most 10 times/second; one badge count per edge/kind/100ms bucket. Maximum 3 concurrent particles per edge; excess increments count.
stream.animation: Accepted request moves source→target, response reverses direction, event uses diamond, processing marks node. Duration 160ms, visual duration never represents latency. Success/check, warning/triangle and failure/cross are static labels after the pulse.
stream.reducedMotion: No particles, pulses or pan animation; update textual count, direction arrow and status icon. Announce terminal/change-of-attention states once; no live-region flood.
stream.unknownTarget: Keep event in activity panel with original IDs; never invent a node or connection.
stream.samplePolicy: demo=true is forbidden on a production feed; mockups always display a persistent sample-data banner.

dashboard.nodeAdmission: Only user-managed objects with an explicit functional role; internal orchestrator, scheduler, queue and helper processes are not user nodes solely because they exist.
dashboard.parity: Every applicable OWNER operation is accessible in an object drawer or workspace panel without navigation away from Dashboard. Administrative sections use the same operation and data.
dashboard.availability: Object capability → current canonical state → input validation → canonical admission. Unsupported object actions hidden; relevant blocked actions visible with localized reason and evidence.
dashboard.permissions: OWNER_FULL; authentication/enrollment boundaries and exact execution contexts remain those in SSOT. No human RBAC or per-secret approvals are introduced.
dashboard.touchKeyboard: Visible Actions button is the equivalent of right click and Shift+F10. Enter/Space opens details, arrows navigate menus, Escape closes and restores focus. Touch uses buttons, never hover-only affordances. Connection creation also offers source/port/target form.
dashboard.help: Each ambiguous control has stable help key, accessible description and focusable help button/popover. Tooltip opens on focus/hover; touch opens the same content explicitly.
dashboard.clipboard: User-gesture clipboard API; failed permission exposes selectable text and Copy retry, never claims copied before promise resolves.
dashboard.previews: CSV/Excel shows typed cells and sheet selection; files expose download and supported preview; email/text shows content and metadata. Formula text is displayed without executing workbook macros or spreadsheet formulas.
dashboard.secretOperations: Use, reveal, create, edit/version, rotate and remove are distinct canonical operations under existing full OWNER authority. Presentation preference must not silently change transport, storage or model access rules.
dashboard.drawerBindingContract: dashboardSurfaceBindings is the exhaustive placement of the UI action registry in Dashboard and chat. Administrative views and Dashboard drawers share the referenced page content and action binding; there is no duplicated form or backend implementation. Object scope is populated only from a compatible selected object; missing required scope opens selection in the drawer. Global actions remain available through Dashboard Actions.

observability.time: ISO 8601 UTC on wire; interpret relative periods once in explicit IANA timezone; echo resolved interval. Sort by recordedAt then canonical sequence/id.
observability.pagination: Opaque cursor binds filters, ordering and snapshot watermark; default 100, maximum 500 per page. Expired cursor returns explicit restart requirement, never silent page omission.
observability.chat: Use canonical structured queries; each factual historical statement links record IDs, interval and provenance. No records in PARTIAL/UNAVAILABLE results does not prove no event occurred.
observability.audit: History read/export uses existing canonical audit requirements and retention. DEBUG follows SSOT 19.3 without changing Secrets policy.
observability.schemaBinding: These schemas define the shared history-query projection used by Dashboard and chat over the listed canonical read operations. They do not authorize additional writes or replace each operation admission contract.
observability.ordering: Filter occurredAt in [fromInclusive,toExclusive); order recordedAt ascending, then eventId ascending using binary UTF-8 ordering. Duplicate eventId is returned once. The opaque cursor freezes this ordering, filters, authorization context and snapshot watermark.
observability.validation: Require fromInclusive < toExclusive and a valid IANA timezone. Resolve relative human times once before the first query; echo the resolved interval. Changing any filter invalidates the cursor and requires an explicit new query. Invalid or expired cursors return HISTORY_CURSOR_INVALID with restart-query action, not an empty success. Other invalid filters return HISTORY_QUERY_INVALID. Normalize an omitted UI limit to 100 before sending the required wire field.
observability.completenessRule: COMPLETE is allowed only when all required sources prove continuous coverage of the resolved interval and snapshot. PARTIAL identifies missingSources and available coverage. UNAVAILABLE returns no items, null coverage bounds and at least one missing source. Empty COMPLETE means no matching records in the evidenced interval; it makes no claim outside that interval.
observability.queryAudit: Record actor execution context, UI/chat origin, normalized filters, snapshot watermark, returned event IDs and completeness through the existing history-access audit operation. Apply the existing SSOT retention, OWNER boundary and Secrets rules to retrieved content.
observability.aggregation: Duration comparisons use completed step spans from the same run and clock domain. Pending spans show elapsed duration with observation time and are excluded from completed-step rankings. Missing start/end evidence is marked incomplete; never infer a zero duration.
observability.provenance: Each historical factual answer identifies eventId/runId, resolved time interval, completeness and source references. Payload content is resolved only through its canonical payloadReference and the same authorized read path as UI.

specification.scope: Specification revision review projection, not a replacement of generation-job lifecycle.

transitions.guard: Canonical precheck PASS for exact digest; required inputs, graph, contracts, integrations and blockers reviewed by OWNER.
OWNER approval of exact unchanged digest; fresh server precheck, compare-and-swap revision and persisted approval evidence.

specification.edit: Any form or chat edit creates a new DRAFT revision and recomputes impact; approval and execution inputs of old revision remain immutable.
specification.generationInput: The job pins approved revisionId+digest and dependency contract digests; mismatch blocks admission.
specification.audit: Persist proposer/channel, base and new digests, changed paths, dependency impact, precheck result and canonical approval event.

multiComponent.proposal: Chat derives component roles from desired outputs, inputs and constraints; server validates and compiles the architecture. OWNER need not choose technologies.
multiComponent.futureDependencies: Address proposed components by stable plan-local IDs and versioned port contracts; absence of runtime instance does not block specification.
multiComponent.cycles: Compute strongly connected components; compile shared interfaces first, build group members against exact interface versions, activate the group only after integration verification. Cyclic build-time prerequisites without a common-interface break are a visible blocker.
multiComponent.order: Topologically sort condensed graph; independent branches may run under bounded canonical concurrency.
multiComponent.partialFailure: Persist per-node attempts, artifacts and outcomes. Halt dependent branches; preserve successful immutable artifacts and run mandatory cleanup. Never claim whole success from partial artifacts.
multiComponent.resume: Revalidate approved digest, input and contract hashes; reuse only verified matching artifacts; reconcile unknown effects before retry.
multiComponent.contractVersioning: Shared contract changes create new immutable versions and invalidate impacted consumer evidence; approval changes require a new specification revision.
multiComponent.done: All required components generated, registered, bound, integration-tested and activated as approved; monitoring and rollback evidence present; no unresolved required child or cleanup.

browser.authority: SSOT 13,14,49,69,70; reuse the single Browser Interaction Plane
browser.mode: Same operation contract for headless and visual managed browser; visual takeover uses existing lease/epoch control.
browser.human: MFA/login/challenge pauses at an evidenced checkpoint; resume only after fresh authenticated page/session verification and current control epoch.
browser.retry: Canonical timeout/deadline and side-effect ledger apply. After possible submission reconcile web result before retry; no duplicate business action on unknown outcome.
browser.evidence: Before/after screenshot references, page/document identity, locator, timestamps and result evidence follow existing retention and Secrets rules.
browser.expiry: Expired session invalidates handles, requests reauthentication and reacquires current page/control state; never silently replay a prior click.
browser.boundary: No bypass of service protection or MFA; external websites remain external systems, managed execution defaults to production Ubuntu.

runtimeTopology.defaultHost: The production Ubuntu environment defined in SSOT hosts the platform and managed generated runtimes unless the approved requirement explicitly selects another deployment target.
runtimeTopology.isolation: Use existing SSOT systemd unit, OS identity, cgroup, filesystem and RuntimeIdentityWire boundaries. Each managed runtime has a separately controlled lifecycle and health identity; do not introduce a second orchestration infrastructure.
runtimeTopology.externalSystems: OpenAI, Meta, Google, email providers and third-party API/web services are external targets, not extra hosting requirements for managed runtimes.
runtimeTopology.secrets: Resolve through existing secret bindings, versions, broker and trusted-perimeter rules. No new restriction or permission is introduced.
runtimeTopology.network: Apply the existing runtime boundary and network-profile contract to ingress and egress; cross-component calls preserve canonical identity, fencing, deadline and correlation.
runtimeTopology.lifecycle: Start, stop, restart, health, recovery and audit use the existing component/runtime operations. A failed member remains separately diagnosable; dependency recovery cannot silently claim whole-system success.
